The '''1984–85 National Hurling League''' was the 54th season of the [[National Hurling League]] (NHL), an annual [[hurling]] competition for the [[GAA county teams]].<ref name="hoganstand1925">{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last= Smith|first=Raymond |date=1999 |title=Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games |location=Dublin, Ireland |page=208 |isbn=0950175870}}</ref> It was won by {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} for the second year in a row.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deiseach.wordpress.com/national-hurling-league-19823/ |title=National Hurling League 1982/3 | Come on the Déise |publisher=Deiseach.wordpress.com |date= |accessdate=2022-02-09 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304202634/https://deiseach.wordpress.com/national-hurling-league-19823/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.adverts.ie/posters/signed-1985-gaa-national-hurling-league-semi-finals-programme-limerick-v-dublin-kilkenny-v-clare/4034087 |title=Signed 1985 GAA National Hurling League Semi-finals Programme Limerick v Dublin & Kilkenny v Clare |website=adverts.ie |access-date=2015-08-24 |archive-date=2016-03-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160318195558/http://www.adverts.ie/posters/signed-1985-gaa-national-hurling-league-semi-finals-programme-limerick-v-dublin-kilkenny-v-clare/4034087 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Division 1==
[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1983-84 National Hurling League|1983-84 season]]. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] entered Division 1 as the promoted teams.

On 14 April 1985, Limerick won the title following a 3-12 to 1-7 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final. It was their second league title in succession and their 9th National League title overall.<ref name="hoganstand1925"/>

Tipperary and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] were relegated from Division 1.

Laois's Eugene Fennelly was the Division 1 top scorer with 2-44.
